title: Touring the Midwest with the Chautauqua marimba band
summary: The group of older multi-instrumentalists plays tents in Peru, Indiana, and Lincoln, Illinois, moving every week like a circus.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, explain one thing to me. What were the instruments, how many were there?
Everybody played -- they had three or four of them across the stage. Besides the others --
Oh.
-- they'd double. Like a trumpet player played trumpet and he played the marimba xylophone.
Oh, I see.
And saxophone player he played em -- bass player played them, the drummer played, and then all of us would go up, but I was just the steady one, see?
Yeah.
It was good.
How old were they?
Oh, they were older than I was.
Yeah.
I think I was 17.
And they were in their 20's, or something?
Oh, yeah. One of them, Forrest of course, was married -- he was 20, something.
And they were a professional group that was being paid?
Oh, yeah. Yeah. So I got paid, too, you know, I mean it was a job, which I was very happy about.
Well what -- what was the job exactly? Where did you play? Where and back?
All over the Midwest. We played Peru, Indiana. We played Lincoln, Illinois --
AAfternoon concerts?
-- we played all these little towns --
Yeah, with the afternoon and evening concerts --
Yeah, the tents would be set up --
I see.
-- they'd move the tent every week from a different town --
I get it -- I get it yeah.
And you'd just keep going around, do you follow?
Yes, I do follow, sure.
Just like a circus.
Yeah, sure. So -
